title: Between the Thomists and the later theologians
source_text: CXLIV. Unde patet hunc Doctorem nolle eandem esse entitatem realem gratiae sufficientis, & gratiae efficacis; sed gratiam efficacem novum auxilium ad sufficientem addere, quod conversionem hominis praeveniat: qua in re ad Thomistas recentiores accedit, & dissentit a Molina, & authoribus gratiae congruae: Et simul tamen eum nolle efficaciam gratiae divinae esse absolutam, sed pendere ab usu liberi nostri arbitrii, qua in re deserit Thomistas, & ad Theologos istos posteriores accedit.
pass_a_gloss: CXLIV. Whence it is clear that this Doctor will not have the real entity of sufficient grace, & of efficacious grace be the same; but that efficacious grace adds a new aid to the sufficient, which precedes the conversion of the man: in which matter he approaches the recent Thomists, & dissents from Molina, & the authors of congruous grace: And at the same time however that he will not have the efficacy of divine grace be absolute, but depend on the use of our free choice, in which matter he deserts the Thomists, & approaches those later Theologians.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXLIV. Clearly, then, this doctor denies that sufficient and efficacious grace are the same real entity. Efficacious grace, for him, adds to sufficient grace a new aid that comes before the person's conversion; here he sides with the recent Thomists and parts from Molina and the authors of congruous grace.

Yet at the same time he denies that the efficacy of divine grace is absolute, making it depend instead on the use of our free choice; here he leaves the Thomists and sides with those later theologians.
